To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the soft-gluon and hard-pole mechanisms for single-transvers spin asymmetries become identical for the quark-gluons correlations, (2) the soft-fermionic-pole and hard pole mechanisms become identical for the gluon-quark correlations, and (3) the two mechanisms become consistent with each other for both quark-gluonic and gluon-quark correlation functions.

the twist-three and Sivers mechanisms for single-spin effects become identical in a specific kinematical regime, and that the twist-three contributions are not independent but rather are related to each other and to the Sivers mechanism by the requirement of mutual consistency.

the two widely-used mechanisms, based on twist-three contributions and Sivers functions, become identical in a certain kinematical regime and, furthermore, that the contributions from soft-fermions and another twist-three correlation function also become consistent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relation between two mechanisms for the single-transverse-spin dependence of semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering.
the relation between two mechanisms for the single-spin asymmetry in semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering.
the relation between twist-three contributions and transverse-momentum distributions in the nucleon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the kinematical regime where the two mechanisms overlap, they are indeed identical.
the two widely-used mechanisms become identical for all twist-three correlation functions in the kinematical regime where the Sivers function is known to be zero.
, at the leading twist-three order, the Sivers mechanism and the twist-three mechanism are identical.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Sivers effect is the only mechanism for spin asymmetries in semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering, and the twist-three contributions are not required.

the two mechanisms for the spin-dependent cross sections in semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering become identical in a certain kinematical regime, which is characterized by a small value of the momentum fraction carried by the final-state parton.
in the kinematical regime where the twist-three contributions dominate over the transverse-momentum dependent parton distributions, the two mechanisms for the single-spin asymmetry become identical.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the kinematical regime under consideration, all of the twist-three contributions to the asymmetries can be expressed in terms of a single twist-three correlation function and the Sivers parton distribution.

the two approaches to single-spin asymmeties are not only consistent with each other but, more importantly, they are complementary to each other in that each of the mechanisms can be applied in a different kinematical regime.
, in the kinematical regime where twist-three contributions are known to be small, the twist-two Sivers effect can be used as a proxy for the full twist-three calculation.
